questions.question: Complete the table for mechanisms of macrolide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae (and group A Streptococcus). For each mechanism state the mechanism of resistance, the gene involved, and whether the organism is also resistant to clindamycin (lincosamide).
questions.question_raw: Fill the table for mechanisms of macrolide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae. Indicate if also resistant to clindamycin (lincosamide).

parts.text: For Streptococcus pneumoniae and group A Streptococcus, for each mechanism (alteration of the macrolide binding site on the bacterial ribosome; active macrolide efflux pumps) state the mechanism of resistance, the gene involved, and clindamycin resistance (yes/no).

parts_raw.text: For strep pneumo and GAS, for each mechanism (alter the macrolide binding site on bacterial ribosome; active macrolide efflux pumps) state the mechanism of resistance, gene involved, and clindamycin resistance (yes/no). [Table also references Staph aureus, but corresponding rows were not preserved in extracted text]

questions.model_answer: (1) Target-site modification: methylation of the 23S rRNA (domain V, adenine A2058) by a ribosomal methylase, reducing binding of macrolides, lincosamides and streptogramin B (MLS-B phenotype); gene = erm (ermB in S. pneumoniae, ermB/ermTR/ermA in GAS); clindamycin resistance = YES (constitutive MLS-B) - may be inducible and detected by D-test. (2) Active efflux: an ATP-driven/major-facilitator efflux pump exports 14- and 15-membered macrolides only (M phenotype), sparing 16-membered macrolides, clindamycin and streptogramins; gene = mef (mefA/mefE in S. pneumoniae, mefA in GAS); clindamycin resistance = NO.
questions.beyond_mandell: Grounded in Mandell (macrolide/lincosamide resistance) and CLSI; the supplied context text is the Parechovirus chapter and does not address this topic.

questions.question: Streptococcus pneumoniae.

parts.text: List 5 phenotypic characteristics of Streptococcus pneumoniae in the microbiology laboratory.

What are the most recent published resistance rates of Streptococcus pneumoniae in Canada to the following drugs: penicillin (meningitis dosing); ceftriaxone (meningitis dosing); erythromycin; moxifloxacin?

parts_raw.text: a) list 5 phenotypic characteristics of S pneumoniae in the microbiology laboratory (2.5)

b) What are the most recent published resistance rates of S pneumoniae in Canada to the following drugs (2): -Penicillin (meningitis dosing); -Ceftriaxone (meningitis dosing); -Erythromycin; -Moxifloxacin

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci/short chains; (2) alpha-hemolytic (green) on blood agar; (3) catalase-negative; (4) optochin (ethylhydrocupreine) susceptible; (5) bile (sodium deoxycholate) soluble - Quellung capsular swelling positive is an acceptable additional feature. b) Using recent Canadian surveillance (CANWARD/CARSS, ~2018-2020): penicillin (meningitis breakpoint, MIC >=0.12) approximately 10-12% non-susceptible; ceftriaxone (meningitis breakpoint) approximately 1-3% non-susceptible; erythromycin/macrolides approximately 25% resistant; moxifloxacin approximately 1% (fluoroquinolone resistance <2%).
questions.beyond_mandell: Rates from Canadian surveillance (CANWARD, CARSS/PHAC) and CLSI breakpoints; the supplied context text is the Parechovirus chapter and does not cover S. pneumoniae, so exact current percentages should be confirmed against the latest CARSS report.

cohort_answer.text: Characteristics: lancet shaped gram positive cocci, capsule, chains, catalase negative, bile soluble, optochin sensitive, Quellung test positive, alpha hemolytic, PYR negative. Resistance rates (CARSS 2020): Penicillin (meningitis dosing) 10-15%; Ceftriaxone (meningitis dosing) 0.7%; Erythromycin 25% (extrapolated from clarithromycin); Moxifloxacin 1% (using ciprofloxacin as proxy)
